label: late original phase / <DEL> after several l,3,2,i,h,p,g tokens
explanation: Fires almost only during the input phase at t>=4 (peak at t=5-7) and on the <DEL> step (99% of mass; nearly never in the copy phase, never at t<2). Within that window it acts like an accumulator over a set of preferred tokens: l is by far the strongest (6.6x rate as input, and the top examples all have l at or just before the peak), followed by 3, 2, i, h, p, g, both as the current input and as the previous one or two inputs. Rate also goes up with the number of digits in the sequence. Activations are largest on or right after an l that follows other preferred tokens, then decay over the next steps and into <DEL>. Requiring 3 or more preferred tokens so far captures about 75% of the mass but precision is only about 0.14, so the real dependence is a graded, recency-weighted sum that no boolean predicate captures well. Does not fire on early inputs (t<3) or on copy-phase outputs.
